name: Event Organization Portal - SIA Project 21 22
description:
Information Systems - academic year 21/22
Course Project
Version 1.0.1 - 20/12/2021
Consider the following scenario:

A startup intends to develop a web portal that can help people who intend to organize an event, bringing together in a single website the information concerning the guests and the various services necessary for the event itself to take place.

The platform to be developed envisages the presence of providers and guests, in addition to the organizer.

At registration, providers supply, in addition to their credentials, their personal data and the data of the company they manage (VAT number, company address, accepted payment methods).

The provider, once registered, will be able to enter the services offered by their company, each belonging to a category (catering, hairdresser, florist etc.), each of which will be associated with a virtual showcase in which the provider can upload demonstration photos, together with the corresponding prices and the hours corresponding to the particular service shown by the showcase (e.g. Hairdresser's blow-dry service has as hours 10:00-12:00 from Tuesday to Thursday, Haircut + shampoo service with hours 8:00-12:00 + 15:00-18:00 from Tuesday to Saturday).

The event organizer, identified by their tax code, at registration, in addition to choosing their credentials, will provide their personal data, residence data and their IBAN for the possible payment of the services.

The organizer, through the portal, will be able to create the event, choosing the type of event (wedding, graduation, concert…) to organize, the date, the place where it will be held and the budget planned for the organization of the event. When creating the event the organizer will be able to choose from a pre-existing list the types of service for which they are interested in receiving help (for example catering, flowers, taxi service etc.).

The organizer will also be able to add the guests to the portal, entering the corresponding data, specifying, in addition to the personal data, the email with which the guest will be identified (and which they will use to log in) and the category to which the guest belongs (relative, friend, colleague etc.).

For each guest added, the system will generate an invitation code that will be sent by email to the specified address; this code will be used by the guest as a password to access the portal.

The organizer will also have available a blog associated with their event in which the organizer or the guests can write information about the event, post photos or videos and leave their thoughts by creating new posts or commenting on the existing ones.

The organizer, once the event has been created, will be able to view, for each service chosen when creating the event, the showcases of the providers that supply the chosen type of service and to arrange an appointment compatible with the hours observed by that service, specifying the details and any special requests. The provider, through their interface, will be able to view the various appointment requests and will have to approve them. The approved requests are displayed directly in a calendar on the site associated with the event, where the organizer will be able to consult the appointments for the agreed services.

After the meeting between the provider and the organizer (in which they agree on the details of the service), the provider calculates the quotation and proceeds to upload the amount on the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once the upload has taken place the organizer can choose whether to accept or reject the quotation; if it is accepted, the total amount is subtracted from the remaining budget. By accepting the amount, the organizer chooses the payment mode (instalments, deposit + balance or full amount) and the payment method (online or on site). If the payment takes place on site the provider will proceed to confirm the amount paid through the portal (in the case of payment in several instalments the provider confirms the amount of each instalment received).

At any time the organizer will be able to consult the history of the contracts (with the related status and cost) and the budget balance for the entire event.
highLevelGoals: The Organizer aims to efficiently create, configure, and manage all aspects of an event, including type, date, location, budget, and required service categories.
The Organizer aims to easily add and manage guests for an event, ensuring they receive invitations and can access event-related information and communication channels.
The Organizer aims to discover suitable service providers, view their offerings, arrange appointments, and manage service agreements and payments within the allocated budget.
The Organizer aims to maintain a clear overview of the event's budget, track expenses, manage quotations, and monitor payment statuses for all contracted services.
The Organizer aims to provide a platform for guests and themselves to share information, photos, videos, and thoughts related to the event through a dedicated blog.
The Provider aims to effectively register their company, manage their service offerings, and create appealing virtual showcases to attract potential organizers.
The Provider aims to efficiently receive, approve, and manage appointment requests from organizers, and to accurately generate and upload quotations for services.
The Provider aims to reliably confirm and track payments received from organizers, especially for on-site payments and installment plans.
The Guest aims to easily access event details and relevant information after receiving an invitation.
The Guest aims to actively participate in event discussions, share content, and leave comments on the event's blog.
lowLevelGoals: The Organizer can initiate the creation of a new event by providing a name and selecting an event type.
The Organizer can specify the date, time, and geographical location for the created event.
The Organizer can set a total budget for the event and allocate funds to different service categories.
The Organizer can add specific service categories (e.g., catering, photography) that are required for the event.
The Organizer can modify existing details of an event, such as date, location, or budget.
The Organizer can add a new guest to an event by providing their email address.
The Organizer can import multiple guests from a provided list (e.g., CSV file) to an event.
The Organizer can send an invitation to selected or all guests for a specific event.
The Organizer can view the RSVP status (e.g., attending, declined, pending) for each invited guest.
The Organizer can remove a guest from the event's guest list.
The Organizer can search for service providers based on service category, location, and availability.
The Organizer can view a service provider's virtual showcase, including their service offerings, portfolio, and reviews.
The Organizer can send an appointment request to a service provider for a specific date and time.
The Organizer can accept a quotation received from a service provider for their services.
The Organizer can initiate a payment for a contracted service, adhering to the agreed payment schedule.
The Organizer can view a summary of the event's budget, including total allocated funds and remaining balance.
The Organizer can record and categorize individual expenses incurred for the event.
The Organizer can view, accept, or reject quotations received from service providers.
The Organizer can check the payment status (e.g., paid, pending, overdue) for each contracted service.
The Organizer can create and publish a new blog post on the event's dedicated communication platform.
The Organizer can upload photos and videos to be included in event blog posts.
The Organizer can view and respond to comments left by guests on event blog posts.
The Provider can create a company profile by providing essential business information.
The Provider can add a new service offering, including its description, pricing, and availability.
The Provider can modify the details of an existing service offering.
The Provider can create and customize a virtual showcase to display their services and portfolio.
The Provider can upload images and videos to their virtual showcase.
The Provider receives notifications for new appointment requests from organizers.
The Provider can approve an incoming appointment request, confirming their availability.
The Provider can decline an incoming appointment request, optionally providing a reason.
The Provider can generate a detailed quotation for their services based on an organizer's request.
The Provider can upload a generated quotation to the system for the organizer to review.
The Provider can confirm the receipt of an on-site payment from an organizer.
The Provider can update the status of installment payments received from organizers.
The Provider can view a history of all payments received for their services.
The Guest can view the core details of an event (date, time, location, description) after receiving an invitation.
The Guest can view the detailed schedule or agenda for the event.
The Guest can respond to an event invitation by confirming or declining their attendance.
The Guest can browse and read posts on the event's dedicated blog.
The Guest can leave comments on individual blog posts within the event's communication platform.
The Guest can upload photos and videos related to the event to the event's blog.
